Scientific Foundation

Our methodologies are built on established geoscience literature. These foundational texts inform the theoretical framework behind TraceSeis services.

The Rock Physics Handbook

Mavko, G., Mukerji, T., & Dvorkin, J.

Cambridge University Press, 2009

Comprehensive reference for rock physics equations and models used throughout our workflows.

Quantitative Seismic Interpretation

Avseth, P., Mukerji, T., & Mavko, G.

Cambridge University Press, 2005

Foundational text on applying rock physics to seismic interpretation - the basis for modern QI workflows.

Quantitative Seismology: Theory and Methods

Aki, K. & Richards, P.G.

W.H. Freeman, 1980

The theoretical foundation for seismic wave propagation and AVO analysis.

Elastic waves through a packing of spheres

Gassmann, F.

Geophysics, 16(4), 673-685, 1951

The original paper establishing fluid substitution theory - still foundational 70+ years later.

Key Concepts

Brief explanations of fundamental concepts that underpin quantitative interpretation.

Rock Physics

The study of relationships between rock composition, pore structure, fluid content, and elastic properties. Rock physics provides the theoretical link between what we measure (seismic) and what we want to know (reservoir properties).

Seismic Inversion

The process of transforming seismic reflection data into quantitative estimates of subsurface properties (impedance, velocity, density). Inversion "removes" the wavelet to reveal the earth's reflectivity and properties.

AVO Analysis

Amplitude Variation with Offset - the study of how seismic amplitude changes with recording angle. AVO provides additional information about rock and fluid properties beyond what post-stack data can reveal.

Gassmann Fluid Substitution

A theoretical framework for predicting how rock elastic properties change when pore fluid changes. Essential for understanding direct hydrocarbon indicators and time-lapse seismic response.

Uncertainty Quantification

The systematic characterization of uncertainty in predictions. In reservoir characterization, this means providing not just a "best estimate" but also confidence intervals that reflect data quality and model limitations.

Lithofacies Classification

The process of assigning rock type (lithofacies) to seismic data based on elastic property patterns. Statistical methods trained on well data enable prediction of lithology away from well control.
